answerlines: Henrik Ibsen (accept An Enemy of the People or En folkefiendebefore “this man” is read)

clues.text: A play by this author follow Dr Stockmann’s investigation of tainted water.
One play by this author ends with a character saying “the sun, the sun."
In one play by this author, the title character is blackmailed by Judge Brack and burns Eilert Lovborg’s manuscript.

One work by this author describes a doctor's attempts to convince his town that its baths are contaminated and another sees Halvard Solness fall from a tower on the top of his home, An Enemy of the People and The Master Builder.
This man’s play Peer Gynt had music written by his fellow Norwegian, Edvard Grieg.
An Enemy of the People is by this author, who created a character who goads Eilert Lovborg into suicide to help her husband, George Tesman.
In another play by this figure, Judge Brack discovers that the title character gave a pistol to her former suitor Eilert Lovberg.
This playwright of When We Dead Awaken wrote about a character who dances the tarantella to distract her husband in another play.
In another play by this author, Torvald patronizingly “forgives” his “little skylark,” causing Nora Helmer to slam the door as she walks out on her family.
Name this Norwegian playwright who wrote about Jørgen Tesman’s wife and Nora Helmer’s escape from the title dwelling in Hedda Gabler and A Doll’s House.
In this play, after a man is asked if he remembers the Gospels, he replies instead that he remembers the coloured maps of the Holy Land.
One character in this play is assumed to be “all of humanity” after he responds to the names “Abel” and “Cain” with cries for help after falling.
In this play, one character tries to tell the Biblical story of the two thieves who hung beside Jesus, bewildering another character.
This work begins with a character struggling with his boots and eventually forgetting them at the end of Act One.
The two main characters of this play discuss whether or not they are in the right place based on the appearance of a leafless tree.
A character in this play says “nothing to be done” while trying to remove his boot.
It is unclear at the end of this play whether the central characters will hang themselves from a solitary tree.
Pozzo and Lucky, blind and dumb respectively, visit the two main characters twice.
The two main characters of this play encounter Pozzo and his slave Lucky before considering hanging themselves from a tree.
Name this play in which Vladimir reminds Estragon that they must do the title action, written by Samuel Beckett.

One character in this work mentions that he would like to plant a garden in his yard after hearing about the “Florida idea,” after which he is reminded of an appointment at Frank’s Chop House later that evening.
In this play, a rubber hose is placed in front of the protagonist by his son, who informs him that he spent three months in jail for stealing a suit in Kansas City.
One character in this work has returned from a vacation in Florida, though another character notes that his mind was not rested.
Originally titled The Inside of His Head, this play includes a scene where Howard Wagner pays more attention to a wire-recording device than to the protagonist.
A distinction in this play is made between people who are “liked” but not “well-liked.”
In this play, a former boss’s fountain pen is among the items stolen by a once-touted high school football star who didn’t retake a math class in order to spite his father.
A pen is impulsively stolen in one scene of this play and a flashback reveals that the titular man had an affair with his receptionist Miss Harvey.
A character from this play who burns his “University of Virginia” sneakers after flunking math recalls running down “eleven flights with a pen in hand,” after stealing that pen from Bill Oliver.
In this play, the title character crashes his car so that his son Biff can use the life insurance money to start his own business.
Name this play in which the title character crashes a car to collect insurance money, written by Arthur Miller.
